Respondents Counsel for the Petitioner : M/s. A. Srinath Counsel for the Respondents : Learned Government Pleader  for Land Acquisition ORDER:
Heard the Learned Counsel for the petitioner.
Also heard the Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, who placed a copy of the written instructions dated 10.10.2023 received from the 3rd respondent for perusal of this Court.

2. The present Writ Petition is filed seeking to declare the action of the respondent authorities in demolishing a part of the business premises of the petitioner in Door No.21/400-1, Madras Road,
Kadapa Town and threatening to demolish the entire premises on the basis of lapsed Land acquisition proceedings under the old Land Acquisition Act, 1894, wherein Award was passed on 30.12.2008 by offering payment under the old Act of 1894 instead of initiating acquisition under the new Land Acquisition Act, 2013 as violative of rights of the petitioner under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013 and for a consequential direction to the respondents to follow the Act, 2013, if so advised for any acquisition of the property of the petitioner for which the petitioner is willing and to pass such other order.
3.

The Learned Counsel for the petitioner with reference to the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 as also the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 2013 raised the contentions to the effect that the acquisition Proceedings in respect of the petitioner's premises situated at D.No.21/400-1,
Kadapa Town have lapsed as the Award has been passed more than 5 years from the date of coming into force of the Act, 2013 on 1.1.2014 combined with the fact that the possession is not taken nor Bepari Umar Saheb vs The State Of Ap on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150889737/

However, the Legal aspects need not be examined in detail in the light of the instructions referred to above, the relevant portion of which reads as follows:-
"....
Again the Municipal Commissioner, Kadapa has given requisition for Land Acquisition for Road widening.
Some of missing cases were brought into the new L.A as per Act 2013.
But the petitioner name was missing in new publication.

Hence the petitioner's land will be acquired as per new LA Act 2013 on par others."
4.

In the light of the above position, the Writ Petition is disposed of, however, with an observation that no coercive action in respect of the subject matter property, shall be resorted to, without following due process of Law.
This order will also not preclude the petitioner and the respondent authorities to negotiate in the matter to arrive at an amicable settlement.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending applications, if any, shall stand closed.
__ JUSTICE NINALA JAYASURYA Date: 11.10.2023
